newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan bank, brokerage units allowed into new areas.
newsitem.headline: Japan bank, brokerage units allowed into new areas.

text.p: Japan's Finance Ministry (MOF) said on Friday it will expand the permissible range of business activities for securities firms' trust banking subsidiaries and banks' securities subsidiaries.
The measures, part of a broad economic deregulation package announced by the government on Friday, will be implemented during the fiscal half-year beginning October 1, MOF said.
Securities subsidiaries set up by banks will be able to act as brokers for equity-related securities, such as convertible bonds, warrant bonds and warrants, and for stock index futures and options.
At the same time, trust banking subsidiaries set up by securities firms will be allowed to enter the loan trust and special fund trust business.

The ministry said in a statement that other currently off-limits activities for bank and brokerage subsidiaries would also be deregulated in the future in line with financial system reforms due to be implemented over the next few years.
The Japanese government plans to liberalise the nation's financial markets by 2001 through a so-called "Big Bang" reform package.

Industry sources said securities firms' trust banking units have also been eager to compete for pension fund business, but rules barring them from that field were not addressed in Friday's deregulation package.
Banks' securities units, for their part, have been keen to expand into stock underwriting and the brokerage business, but these areas were also left untouched.
Banks and securities firms began moving onto each other's turf through wholly owned subsidiaries after financial reforms that took effect in 1993.
The subsidiaries' permissible range of activities was strictly limited, however, to dampen the impact of increased competition on firms already doing business in those areas.
